newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jailed for mad cow disease extortion attempt.
newsitem.headline: German jailed for mad cow disease extortion attempt.

text.p: A German who tried to extort millions of marks from Swiss Nestle's Maggi unit by threatening to inject its food products with mad cow disease was jailed for three years and two months on Friday.
The man, identified as Rainer M., said heavy debts had led him to seek to extort money from the company earlier this year.
A court in the southern town of Konstanz handed his wife, Gabriele M., a one-year suspended sentence for her part in the crime.
Mad cow disease, known scientifically as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), is a fatal cattle brain disease that scientists have said could be passed to humans.

The sentence comes as German police investigated a new extortion attempt on Thomy, a sister company of Maggi within the multinational Nestle food group. It received a letter earlier this week claiming that its products in stores around the country had been contaminated.

Police said on Friday they would no longer be briefing media on the progress of their enquiries to help in the investigation. On Thursday they said examinations on products had so far produced no evidence of contamination.
